This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `104b2bd8a01deb962589ad121f1437e83a9d8d97` — the merge of head `bb7403dc0e213e5b0ae4f88d7789c74a9e4e706d` into base `c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 104b2bd8a01deb962589ad121f1437e83a9d8d97 && git checkout 104b2bd8a01deb962589ad121f1437e83a9d8d97
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7 bb7403dc0e213e5b0ae4f88d7789c74a9e4e706d && git checkout -B drift-repro c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7 && git merge --no-ff bb7403dc0e213e5b0ae4f88d7789c74a9e4e706d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9241122bac0eda48d119b21a0719812e5928cb1e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + none (the test file and the changeset are the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; both were read)

Inputs read: card #32477 body and all 4 comments (triage 6810245563, claim 6810478250, step-0 ruling 6810557307, os-dev-report 6811805332); PR #32495 body, file list (3 files, +249/-1) and the net diff against `main` (`c110853e`). Code read outside the diff, not reviewed: `resolveArtifactCollections` (`packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts`), `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` (`packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts`), `refuseCoOwnedObjectNameCollision` and `computeFQN` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`), and in `stack.zod.ts` `composeBuiltStacks`, `collectComposedActionKeyCollisions`, `composedBodyHolder`, `preservePackageEntries`, `assemblePackageBody`, `packagesReproduceComposedCollections`.

Check-runs on this head, at review time. The PR is still a draft.
- Ran, success: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Flag docs affected by code changes, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three Lint · scoped runs, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Build UI Deps, both shard planners, Auto Label, filter.
- Not finished (in_progress, no verdict): Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16. The suite that holds the 11 new pins (Test Core) has no CI verdict yet; the dev's 56/56 is a self-report only.
- Skipped: Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict, Build Docs, Lint UI, Dogfood Verify CLI, the matrix Dogfood gate, UI Published Artifacts, Temporal Conformance, the two opt-in harnesses, Schedule gate.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Newly refused, every strategy and either manifest: right.** `refuseNestedBodyObjectConflicts` takes no strategy and no manifest option and runs at the end of `mergeObjects` (step 2). It throws `StackComposeObjectConflictError` (422 `STACK_COMPOSE_OBJECT_CONFLICT`) when one name is declared by two or more distinct inputs and at least one declaration is a body's. This is option A.
- **Flat inputs byte-identical: right.** The existing walk is untouched and runs first, so its refusals and texts win. An input without an array `packages` adds only top-level notes, and a name enters the refusal set only through a body, so flat-only compositions cannot reach the new throw. The helper mutates nothing.
- **Body objects never lifted: right.** The helper returns void; `result` and `actionsOwner` are not touched.
- **Holder identity: right.** It reuses #32475's own `composedBodyHolder` (`id || name`, empty namespace is none), not a second spelling. The body is read at `entry.manifest`, as step 6 reads it.
- **Top level claims a name over its bodies: right against the ruling.** `claimed` is seeded from the input's own top-level names, so a body object whose own input's top level carries the name is never noted as a body declaration. The first body per name stands for the input.
- **Nested + nested, and the same holder: right.** The test is on distinct input indexes only, never on holders, so two nested inputs, the same nested artifact twice, and flat `p1` beside an artifact that carries `p1` are all refused.
- **Exports, schema shape, api-surface: none moved.** One private interface and one private function; no `export` line in the diff, no generated baseline in the file list. The only public-facing text change is the `composeStacks` jsdoc.

### ② Semver level

Matches the ruling and the diff. The changeset is `@objectstack/spec` minor, carries a `**BREAKING**` banner, FROM/TO in the Fix bullet, and exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and `Skills-docs: none` are on both the changeset and the PR body. The diff publishes a narrowing only, in `@objectstack/spec` alone, so no other package needs a bump. Check Changeset: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. `out_of_scope_findings`: empty. `security_findings`: none.
- The three deviations (PR-body line order, branch started from #32475's head then merged `main`, harness generated-with lines) are process only and are answered: the net diff against `main` is the card's three files, and PR-body guards passed.
- Escalated to the seat (found in this review, outside this diff; read from the code, not run):
  1. **Additive nested input under `override` / `merge`.** An input that carries BOTH a top-level `X` and a body `X` (a preserve artifact that was not stripped: one package entry, or a manifest-less sibling) beside a flat `X` is judged by the flat walk alone, as the ruling orders. Under `override` / `merge` it still composes, and the body keeps its own `X`. The boot registers bodies through `resolveArtifactPackageOrder`, not through the top-level-first merge, so by the mechanism step 0 measured this is the same refuse-or-trim outcome. Step 6 also skips that body object's embedded actions as already judged. So the PR body's claim that step 6's skip premise is now true holds for every body object its input's top level does not claim, and not for this shape.
  2. **Flat pair under `preserve` with `override` / `merge`.** `preservePackageEntries` assembles each body from its input unchanged, and the additive top level stays because the bodies do not reproduce it. The artifact then carries `p1`'s and `q`'s bodies both declaring `X`: the shape step 0 measured as DUPLICATE_ARTIFACT_OBJECT_NAME at boot. Pre-existing on `main`; it feeds finding 1 in ④.
  Both want a step-0 style measurement and a card of their own; neither is a defect of this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`: the change holds against the ruling and the code it cites. Attempts to break it:

- Body object whose own input's top level claims the name: not judged as a body declaration (`claimed` seed). Holds.
- Two nested inputs: refused, one issue naming both bodies. Holds.
- Same package twice: refused (distinct input indexes). Holds.
- Embedded `X:approve` pair: refused at step 2, before step 6 runs; step 6 is unchanged. Holds.
- Ordering: only the provenance check, the 0/1-input early returns, options parse and `selectManifest` precede step 2. The flat walk's own refusals fire first with their old text. Nothing is concatenated, preserved or written before the new throw, and it passes through the same `withRefusalConversions` wrapper.
- Malformed shapes: a non-array `objects` is already refused by the walk; a non-array `packages`, a non-record entry or body, and a nameless object are skipped, and step 3 keeps its own refusal for a malformed `packages`. No bare TypeError path.
- Over-refusal: `computeFQN` returns the short name, so object names are one flat space and the bare-name comparison matches the registry's. The measured rows are the co-owner pair; a namespace-less pair is not measured, but the flat door already refuses that pair by bare name.

Findings:

1. **should-fix: the third remedy is not true under `manifest: 'preserve'`.** The refusal text and the changeset's Fix bullet say to compose the packages as flat inputs "so the objectConflict strategy can reconcile them". Under `'error'` the flat pair is refused too. Under `override` / `merge` with `preserve` (the mode that produces nested artifacts) the composed artifact still carries both bodies declaring the name, which by step 0's measured mechanism the boot refuses (escalation 2 above). The remedy holds only under the default manifest with `override` / `merge`. Read, not run. Either scope the sentence to what is true, or measure the flat `preserve` + `override` boot and word the remedy from the result. The remedies "rename" and "`objectExtensions`" read true (`objectExtensions` is the authorable key for extending another package's object). `Skills-docs: none` rests on this text carrying the prescription, so its truth is part of the contract.
2. **nit: two ruling rows have no pin.** The same holder on both sides (flat `p1` beside an artifact carrying `p1`, or one artifact twice), and the top-level-claims rule (an input with both a top-level and a body `X` beside another declarer, judged as `main` judges it). Both are correct at this head by construction. The existing pins (three modes x two manifests x both orders, embedded approve, nested + nested, two controls) match the ruling.
3. **nit: the stack label of a nested input is its last input's manifest id** (`'com.example.p2' (stack #0)` for a declaration in `p1`'s body). The holder suffix disambiguates it.
4. **nit: the `composeStacks` jsdoc says "a multi-package artifact"**, while the door reads any input carrying `packages[]`.

No must-fix. Finding 1 earns a delta review of its fix. The Test Core, Build Core and Type Check · workspace verdicts were not in at review time and gate the queue independently of this record.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bb7403dc0e213e5b0ae4f88d7789c74a9e4e706d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/compose-stacks.test.ts, .changeset/32477-compose-nested-artifact-object-bodies.md (delta `9241122b..bb7403dc`, one commit, 3 files, +29/-5)

Inputs read: contract review 6811982973; the delta diff; the changeset at the head; in `stack.zod.ts` at the head `mergeObjects`, `refuseNestedBodyObjectConflicts`, `refuseUnmergeableCollections`, `selectManifest`, `preservePackageEntries`, `packagesCarryEveryInputCollection`, `assemblePackageBody`, `stackLabel`, the `manifest` option jsdoc and step 1/3a/8 of `composeBuiltStacks`; the nested-artifact `describe` block of `compose-stacks.test.ts` at the head.

Check-runs on this head, at review time. The PR is still a draft.
- Failed: none.
- Success: Check PR Size, Auto Label, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards (both runs), both shard planners, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, filter. One Check Changeset run succeeded.
- Still running (no verdict): Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, and a second Check Changeset run.
- Skipped: Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict, Build Docs, Dogfood Verify CLI, the matrix Dogfood gate, UI Published Artifacts, Temporal Conformance, the two opt-in harnesses, Schedule gate.
- The suite holding the pins (Test Core) has never returned a CI verdict on this PR: the shards were cancelled on `9241122b` and are in progress here. The two new pins are judged below by reading only.

### ① Derived judgments

Delta only; carries 6811982973 for the rest.

- **No logic moved: confirmed.** The `stack.zod.ts` hunks change one string literal (the refusal message tail) and one jsdoc sentence. No condition, no call, no export, no issue string (`issues[]` is untouched, so the existing pins' expectations stand). The test hunk adds two `it` blocks and changes none.
- **Accept set unchanged** from `9241122b`.

### ② Semver level

Delta only; carries 6811982973. The changeset is still `@objectstack/spec` minor with the `**BREAKING**` banner, the three declaration lines and the one `adr-0087` marker, all untouched. Only the banner sentence and the Fix bullet changed.

### ③ Boundary flags

Delta only; carries 6811982973, including its two escalations (additive nested input under `override` / `merge`; flat pair under `preserve` with `override` / `merge`). The delta neither closes nor widens either. Nothing new to escalate.

### ④ Design judgment

**S1 (should-fix of 6811982973): answered.** Each sentence of the refusal text, against the head:

- "compose the packages as flat inputs ... under the default manifest with `override` or `merge`, which fold the two into one object": true. A flat input has no `packages`, so the walk in `mergeObjects` is the only judge; `override` replaces the entry in place and `merge` spreads it, leaving one object. The default manifest is `'last'` (`selectManifest`), step 3a emits `packages` only under `'preserve'`, so the output carries one declaration and no body.
- "Under `{ manifest: 'preserve' }` each package keeps its own body, so there only the first two remedies apply": true. `preservePackageEntries` pushes `assemblePackageBody(stack)` for each input with a manifest, and that copies the input's own collections unchanged, so both bodies still declare the name whatever the strategy did to the top level. Under `'error'` the flat pair is refused by the walk, and the text no longer offers `'error'`.
- Rename: still true (the door compares bare names). `objectExtensions`: still true. It is the authored stack key "Extensions to objects owned by other packages", composed by concat, and it declares no object, so neither door sees a second declaration.
- The changeset's Fix bullet says the same three things with the same scoping. True.

**Nit 2 (two pins): added, and both assert what they claim.**
- Same holder: `composeStacks([nested(), p1()])`. `nested()` has no top-level objects, so the walk finds nothing; the body door notes `alpha_shared` and `alpha_p1_item` in `packages[0]` (holder `p1`, namespace `alpha`) and at `stack.objects[0]` / `[1]` of stack #1. Two issues, in body insertion order, with the labels the pin expects (`'com.example.p2' (stack #0)`, `'com.example.p1' (stack #1)`). The `.replace` on `issueFor('nested-first')` hits its target string exactly once.
- Top-level-claims control: `composeStacks([p1(), loose], { manifest: 'preserve' })` yields one package entry (`loose` has no manifest), so `packagesCarryEveryInputCollection` is false and the additive shape stays: `alpha_shared` at top level and in `p1`'s body, as the two setup assertions state. Beside `q()` under `'error'` the existing walk throws first with `main`'s text `object 'alpha_shared' is defined in multiple stacks.` Correct.

**Nit 4 (jsdoc): answered.** The jsdoc reads "Any input carrying `packages[]` (a nested artifact)"; the changeset banner reads "an input carrying `packages[]` (a nested artifact)". They agree.

Findings, all on the delta:

1. **nit: the control does not discriminate the `claimed` seed.** Under `'error'` the walk throws before `refuseNestedBodyObjectConflicts` runs, so deleting `const claimed = new Set(topLevel)` leaves this pin green. It pins "the walk's refusal and text win", which is what its title says, and not the top-level-claims rule itself. Only an `override` / `merge` call would discriminate, and that is the shape of escalation 1 in 6811982973, still unmeasured. Leaving it unpinned until that is ruled is defensible.
2. **nit: "which fold the two into one object" is loose for both strategies.** `override` replaces the earlier declaration whole (the same message says two sentences earlier that `'override'` replaces and `'merge'` folds), and `merge` refuses with `STACK_COMPOSE_COLLECTION_CONFLICT` when the two declare a non-`fields` collection or config object differently (two objects each embedding `actions`, for one). That refusal carries its own remedy, and the `manifest` option's jsdoc already uses "fold" for both, so no reader is misled into a dead end.
3. **nit: the jsdoc's new subject is slightly wider than the door.** "Any input carrying `packages[]` ... an object name one of those bodies declares and another input declares too is refused under every strategy" omits the qualifier the changeset's Now bullet keeps ("and its input's own top level does not"). For an additive input the name is judged by the strategy. The old wording ("a multi-package artifact") had the same omission, since a multi-package artifact can be additive too, so the delta did not introduce it. Tied to escalation 1.

No must-fix, no should-fix. The delta answers S1, nit 2 and nit 4 of 6811982973; nit 3 there (stack label of a nested input) is unchanged and stays a nit. Test Core, Build Core and Type Check · workspace have no verdict yet and gate the queue independently of this record.
